plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Exit QQQ, QQQI, SMH, and CRWD to reduce sector concentration.
Buy MSFT as a quality tech addition.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces leverage.
It aims for lower volatility and a smaller cash buffer.
conservative.read: This plan focuses on capital preservation with lower expected monthly returns. Risk is significantly reduced by cutting leverage and concentrated tech exposure, aiming for a steadier, less volatile outcome.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to minimal levels.
Sell QQQ, QQQI, and SMH to reduce sector concentration.
Buy SNOW, a top scanner setup, for growth potential.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
It aims for moderate returns with controlled leverage.
balanced.read: This balanced approach aims for risk-first growth, targeting moderate monthly returns. Leverage is kept low, and concentration is reduced while adding a promising scanner setup. Expect a moderate level of volatility.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to target levels.
Sell QQQ, QQQI, and SMH to free up capital.
Buy SNOW, a high-potential scanner setup, for growth.
This plan aggressively pursues growth through leverage and concentration.
It accepts higher potential upside and downside risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan aims for high growth by increasing leverage and concentrating on strong setups. Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns and the risk of rapid losses, especially with leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta tech (CRWD).
Exit QQQ and SMH to reduce volatility.
Increase QQQI to 30% for income generation.
Trim SPY to maintain some broad market exposure.
This plan prioritizes steady income and low drawdown.
income.read: This income-focused plan aims for steady monthly distributions with minimal drawdown. It shifts capital away from growth and leverage towards income-generating assets like QQQI. While distributions are prioritized, NAV can still decline in market downturns.
